AS400:update_policy_address.label: AS/400
AS400:update_policy_address.description: Change the risk address held against a POLMAST record — address lines, town or city, county and postcode. Every other field on the policy is left as it was. Uses the local IBM i (AS/400) enterprise mock API.

S3:list_buckets.label: AWS S3
S3:list_buckets.description: List every S3 bucket the configured AWS credentials can see, with the region each one was created in. Use this to discover bucket names before working on objects.

S3:list_objects.label: AWS S3
S3:list_objects.description: List the objects in a bucket, newest page first. Narrow the result with 'prefix' to look inside one folder, and set 'delimiter' to '/' to get folder names back as prefixes instead of every nested key. Pass the returned 'next_token' back in to read the following page.

S3:get_object_metadata.label: AWS S3
S3:get_object_metadata.description: Check whether an object exists and read its size, MIME type, last modified date and storage class without downloading the body. Use this before reading, overwriting or deleting a key.

S3:get_object.label: AWS S3
S3:get_object.description: Read the contents of one object. Text files come back as plain text, anything else as base64. Objects larger than 5 MB are refused - use S3:download_url for those instead.

S3:put_object.label: AWS S3
S3:put_object.description: Write an object, creating it or overwriting whatever is already at that key. Give text in 'content', or binary in 'content_base64'. Writing to an existing key replaces it, so read it first if the old version still matters.

S3:copy_object.label: AWS S3
S3:copy_object.description: Copy an object to another key, optionally into a different bucket. The source is left untouched. Use this to duplicate a file or to take a backup before overwriting one.

S3:move_object.label: AWS S3
S3:move_object.description: Move or rename an object: copy it to the new key, then delete the original. S3 has no native rename, so this is how a key gets changed. The source is only deleted once the copy has succeeded.

S3:delete_object.label: AWS S3
S3:delete_object.description: Permanently delete one object. On a bucket without versioning this cannot be undone, so confirm the key with S3:get_object_metadata first. S3 reports success even when the key never existed.

S3:download_url.label: AWS S3
S3:download_url.description: Create a time limited download link for an object, so a person can fetch it without AWS credentials. Use this for large files and for anything that should be handed to a customer, instead of reading the body with S3:get_object.

S3:upload_url.label: AWS S3
S3:upload_url.description: Create a time limited upload link, so someone can PUT a file straight into the bucket without AWS credentials. Use this when the file is too large to pass through S3:put_object or is not yet in hand.

S3:upload_file.label: AWS S3
S3:upload_file.description: Upload a file that is already on this machine's filesystem into the bucket, reading it straight off disk. Use this for a file another system handed over as a path, instead of reading the bytes yourself and passing them to S3:put_object. Give 'key' to choose where it lands; without one the file keeps its own name under the configured prefix.

CHEM:mol_to_sdf.label: Chemistry
CHEM:mol_to_sdf.description: Convert one or more MOL blocks (V2000 or V3000) into a single SDF document. Several molfiles pasted one after another become several SDF records, and SDF given as input keeps the data fields it already carries. The atom and bond blocks are passed through untouched - no chemistry is inferred, nothing is re-computed. Returns the SDF as text; write it somewhere with S3:put_object if it needs to be stored.

TELCO:pcm_to_wav.label: Telco
TELCO:pcm_to_wav.description: Convert all PCM audio files (.pcm) in a directory to WAV format

TELCO:transcribe_meeting.label: Telco
TELCO:transcribe_meeting.description: Transcribe WAV audio files in a directory with the self-hosted ASR service, write each transcript as a .txt file next to the audio, and return the individual and combined transcripts. Speaker recordings can be skipped when only the mixed meeting transcript is needed. Existing .txt files in the directory are reused, so re-running on the same meeting does not transcribe a second time.

TELCO:summarize_meeting.label: Telco
TELCO:summarize_meeting.description: Summarize a full meeting transcript into a structured Turkish summary: an overall summary paragraph and the highlights. Works from the combined transcript alone, with no per-speaker recording, and deliberately produces no next steps

TELCO:summarize_meeting_by_speaker.label: Telco
TELCO:summarize_meeting_by_speaker.description: Summarize a meeting into a structured Turkish summary: an overall summary paragraph, the highlights, and the next steps. Receives both the combined transcript and each participant's own recording, so statements and next step owners are attributed to the right speaker

TELCO:judge_summary.label: Telco
TELCO:judge_summary.description: Evaluate meeting notes with a Turkish LLM judge prompt. Returns 0-100 scores for the meeting summary, next steps, topics, highlights, overall quality and accuracy, plus a short Turkish justification. Next steps are not evaluated for variant A because that variant does not generate them.

TELCO:prepare_meeting_attachments.label: Telco
TELCO:prepare_meeting_attachments.description: Write the full meeting transcript, each speaker's transcript and the LLM judge's evaluation to .txt files on disk, and return them as a list of email attachment descriptors ({ filename, path }) that can be passed straight to GREY:send_email or TELCO:send_email_ews. Meeting audio is NOT attached unless includeAudio is explicitly turned on

TELCO:resolve_participants.label: Telco
TELCO:resolve_participants.description: Replace participant IDs with their real names, anywhere they appear (recursively) inside a text transcript or a structured summary object, using a participants list from metadata

TELCO:translate.label: Telco
TELCO:translate.description: Translate text from a source language into a target language using a local LLM. Returns the translated text only.
